test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 16 Feb 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is NOT an instrument of the monetary policy of the Reserve Bank of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Goods and Services Tax(GST)**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Goods and Services Tax (GST)** is NOT an instrument of the monetary policy of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).
 
• GST is a comprehensive indirect tax on the manufacture, sale, and consumption of goods and services throughout India.
 
• The primary objective of GST is to consolidate multiple indirect taxes into a single tax to simplify the taxation process and ensure a uniform tax rate across the country.
 
• On the other hand, the instruments of the monetary policy of the RBI include the Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR), Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR), and Bank Rate, which are used to control the money supply and interest rates in the economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** is the central banking institution of India, which controls the monetary policy of the Indian rupee.
 
• The RBI was established on **1st April 1935** and was nationalized on **1st January 1949**.
 
• The primary functions of the RBI include regulating the issue of banknotes, maintaining reserves to secure monetary stability, and operating the credit and currency system of the country to its advantage.
 
• Monetary policy involves the management of money supply and interest rates by the central bank to control inflation and stabilize the currency.
 
• Other tools of monetary policy include Open Market Operations (OMO) and the Marginal Standing Facility (MSF).
